ms.criteria:

ms.report:
We have successfully redesigned both data input and output flows - the new design is based on as series of collapsable dashboards enabling data capturing for each phase of wine producing process: winery & vineyards, grapes, bulk wines, bottled wines. For data presentation, we have adopted an approach based on multiple sections enabling presenting the end user with data that is relevant in specific usage contexts: EU label data (allergens and nutrients), sommelier data, winery and wine characteristics, general wine details, full wine details. 
The designs can be located here: 
We have aggregated the list of functionality that is expected from a supply chain tracking system based on interviews and discussions with multiple wineries. While we acknowledge that this might not be a complete list, this is the most exhaustive list we have collected so far and we shall keep this document as living document that will continue to be updated as we navigate this phase of the project. With some exceptions which we didn't plan to address in the first place, we seem to be covering a significant number of requirements. Potential further enhancements could include adding the ability to triangulate data with state agencies to ensure data input by wineries is valid as well as defining a solution for tracking the logistics of bulk / bottled wine.

Redesigned UI/UX for Data Input & Visualization
1. Purpose & Scope
The primary goal of the UI/UX redesign was to turn WineOpSys into a clean, fast, intuitive interface for both operational staff and other users in the wine supply chain. Our design addressed two distinct user categories:
・Winery Admins & Operators: Need fast, accurate tools to input and monitor data for grapes, bulk wine, and bottled wine.
・End Users / Auditors / Partners: Require visually rich and clean dashboards that communicate real-time supply chain state and trends.

This milestone redefined both ends of that spectrum.
2. Core Design Principles
We applied the following product and design principles throughout:
・Clarity Over Complexity – Minimize cognitive load through clean interfaces, limited choices per view, and clear labels.
・Speed to Action – Users can accomplish core tasks (log a harvest, update inventory, generate report) in ≤ 3 clicks.
・Visual Truth – Replace lists with visual data where possible: charts, progress bars, status indicators, color-coded labels.
・Device Flexibility – All UI designed for 1200px+ desktop and 768px+ tablets; touch controls considered from the start.

3. Components Developed
A. Control Panels
Each control panel is a modular dashboard containing:
・Dynamic DataGrid Tables with Inline Actions
・Edit, delete, and duplicate entries in-place.
・Status management (e.g., "Pending", "In Storage", "Dispatched").
・Bulk actions and advanced filters (varietal, batch ID, date ranges).
・Slide-in Form Drawer (MUI Drawer)
・Appears on entry creation or edit.
・Includes dynamic fields.
・Input types: text, autocomplete, select, multi-date picker, file upload (photos, docs)
・Real-time Save Feedback
・Optimistic updates using React: changes appear instantly, sync
